title: Scalar coherence and field descent of clopen exceptional comparisons
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $O=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=O/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\geq1$ [def-pur-conventions]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type between finite-type $k$-schemes, without assuming $Y$ separated over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $I$ be finite and let $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$ be pairwise disjoint open and closed immersions covering $X$, with $g_i=g\circ j_i$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Empty components and the empty cover of $X=\varnothing$ are allowed.

Fix $c=(a,p)$ and $c_i=(a\circ j_i,p)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use the counit-normalized strict-system comparisons $\rho_{i,A}:r_{i,A}G_{g,A}\cong G_{g_i,A}$, their site transports and integral total-limit realizations [lem-pur-clopen-counit-adjoint-comparison, lem-pur-clopen-system-integral-realization]. All operations and rationalized/common-stage categories are the actual constructions of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

For every finite coefficient extension $E\subset E'$ put $O'=\mathcal O_{E'}$, $B_n=O'/\varpi^nO'$ and let $T$ be the finite-free levelwise scalar extension from $A_n$ to $B_n$. Let $s_g:TG_{g,A}\cong G_{g,B}T$ and $s_{g_i}$ be the prescribed coherent system scalar comparisons of [lem-pur-etale-coefficient-system-adjoint]. Under $Tr_{i,A}\cong r_{i,B}T$, one has the equality of derived-system natural transformations
$$s_{g_i}\circ T(\rho_{i,A})=(\rho_{i,B}T)\circ r_{i,B}(s_g).$$
The corresponding left-adjoint open-extension squares are the sectionwise scalar-extension squares, and this equality uses their adjunction mates with the prescribed counits. The equality includes the cofinal identification $\varpi^nO'=(\varpi')^{e(E'/E)n}O'$, where $\varpi'$ is a uniformizer of $O'$. It respects identity and successive extensions with their tensor associators. The integral comparison is $O$-linear; the scalar squares pass through $DU$ and the actual $R\lim$ realization. Rationalizing gives $Lj_i^*Rg_E^!\cong R(g_i)_E^!$. These isomorphisms agree after every common finite extension and define a natural isomorphism $Lj_i^*Rg_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}^!\cong R(g_i)_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}^!$ in the common-stage category, independent of the representative of a morphism. Evaluation at the coefficient unit gives the same scalar-compatible comparisons for the dualizing objects $\omega_g=Rg^!\Lambda_Y$. For an empty component all these comparisons are the unique map between zero objects.

proof.text: Use the strict-system restriction, zero insertion, insertion counit $c_i$ and open compositor defining $b_{i,A}$ from [lem-pur-clopen-strict-system-support]. The local-field stage lemma gives finite free $B_n/A_n$ using one $O$-basis of $O'$ at every level. Consequently $T$ is exact. The comparisons $T E_{i,A}\cong E_{i,B}T$ and $T r_{i,A}\cong r_{i,B}T$ are componentwise distributivity. The insertion counit is identity on component $i$ and zero on the others, so tensoring carries it to the same counit. For the open compositor, both routes send a generator $m\otimes b$ on $X_i$ to that same generator in $(a\circ j_i)_!T M$ and send it to zero off the component. The formulas commute with restrictions and with $m\otimes b\mapsto t(m)\otimes\bar b$ for a quotient transition $t$. Hence these are equal maps of strict systems before localization, also on complexes. This is the sectionwise scalar-extension square (Stacks Tags 03DI, lemma-extension-by-zero, and 03DJ, lemma-extension-by-zero-exact, sites-modules.tex).

source.place: Construction 5.15, open part; the section formula is Stacks 03DI/03DJ.

proof.text:
Write $q_g:T_YF_{g,A}\cong F_{g,B}T_X$ and $q_{g_i}:T_YF_{g_i,A}\cong F_{g_i,B}T_i$ for [lem-pur-etale-system-coefficient-projection]. They are specified by coefficient-adjunction transposition of $F$ applied to $m\mapsto m\otimes1$ followed by the restriction/direct-image identification. Under $T_XE_{i,A}\cong E_{i,B}T_i$, this gives
$$q_{g_i}\circ T_Yb_{i,A}=(b_{i,B}T_i)\circ(q_gE_{i,A}).$$
Indeed transpose the two sides under coefficient extension/restriction. The restriction identification for $Rp_*$ is the SAME in both, since the proper part $p$ is shared. What remains is the open-extension identity from step 1 and naturality of $m\mapsto m\otimes1$ with its compositor. Thus the transposes agree; injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves the equation. This calculation is with actual system transformations, using the projection node's resolution-independent map action; it does not deduce equality from finite evaluations.

source.place: Construction 5.15 and Lemma 5.16; scalar-unit normalization of the system projection.

proof.text:
The counit-normalized $\rho_{i,A}$ is the conjugate of $b_{i,A}^{-1}:F_{g_i,A}\to F_{g,A}E_{i,A}$ for the composite adjunction $F_{g,A}E_{i,A}\dashv r_{i,A}G_{g,A}$ and $F_{g_i,A}\dashv G_{g_i,A}$: its transpose is exactly the insertion/exceptional counit equation in [lem-pur-clopen-counit-adjoint-comparison]. The prescribed $s_g$ and $s_{g_i}$ are the mates of $q_g^{-1}$ and $q_{g_i}^{-1}$: their transpose is $T\varepsilon\circ q^{-1}$ by [lem-pur-etale-system-scalar-mate-coherence]. Take mates of step 2, including the insertion adjunction and its scalar-compatible counit from step 1. The pasting-along-adjunctions and change-of-adjunction formulas of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] identify the two mates with
$$s_{g_i}\circ T\rho_{i,A},\qquad (\rho_{i,B}T)\circ r_{i,B}s_g.$$
The mates are equal because the left squares are equal. This proves the requested derived-system equation with the prescribed counits, rather than choosing new right-adjoint isomorphisms.

source.place: Construction 5.15 and adjunction after Lemma 5.16; Lemma 5.22; mate pasting for the open compositor.

proof.text: For the identity coefficient extension every balancing map in step 1 is the tensor-unit map, and the scalar mate is identity. For $E\subset E'\subset E''$, both iterated sectionwise scalar maps send $((m\otimes b)\otimes c)$ to $m\otimes bc$; the projection and scalar-mate composition equations therefore give the same square under the canonical tensor associators. The stage lemma gives $\varpi^nO'=(\varpi')^{en}O'$ with $e\geq1$. Apply [lem-pur-etale-system-cofinal-mate] to $r(n)=en$. Its comparison preserves counits and its left-extension comparison is formed from the same coefficient projections. Restriction to these indices commutes with the componentwise open compositor in step 1. Mate pasting therefore carries step 3 to this cofinal identification, also under further subsequences. These statements concern the entire systems and their maps, not only their values at individual levels.

source.place: Construction 4.1 and Constructions 5.14–5.15; scalar associators and cofinal counit comparison.

proof.text: Transport step 3 by the actual system functors $\nu_{X,A}^*(-)R\nu_{Y,A,*}$ of [lem-pur-clopen-system-integral-realization], and precompose with the actual reduction functor $\mathcal R_Y$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. This preserves the equality. To identify the scalar comparisons here, choose one $O$-basis of $O'$: levelwise $T$ is a fixed finite direct sum, so it commutes with the additive system site functors on complexes and derived morphisms. The canonical comparison is the balancing map, independent of this basis. Reduction commutes with extension by the map $(x\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes ab$ on one K-flat reduction representative, with inverse $x\otimes b\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes b$. These maps commute with all quotient transitions and chain maps. Forgetting the finite coefficient action to completed coefficients retains these maps and their equality. Thus step 3 gives the scalar square for the actual transported exceptional reduction systems before total inverse limit.

source.place: Constructions 5.15/5.22 with the actual reduction, site transport and DU construction.

proof.text:
Put $R_W=\widehat O_W$, $S_W=\widehat {O'}_W$. These sheaves are finite free and ordinary $-\otimes^L_{R_W}S_W$ agrees naturally with the prescribed integral scalar extension on complete inputs by [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Apply the canonical natural comparison $C R\lim\cong R\lim C^{\mathrm{Tow}}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-strict-tower-transport] to the whole square in step 5. On the $n$th output its tensor comparison is the canonical balanced identification
$$(DU_A M_n)\otimes_{R_W}S_W\cong DU_B(M_n\otimes_{A_n}B_n),$$
because $S_W/\varpi^nS_W=(B_n)_W$ and $M_n$ is an $A_n$-module. The quotient identification is the completed coefficient reduction used in the stated scalar-comparison construction. Naturality of the total-limit comparison preserves the equality and both inverses. The integral $\rho_i$ is exactly this realized system arrow by [lem-pur-clopen-system-integral-realization]. All its constituents are $O$-linear: the system $\rho$ is $O$-linear, $DU$ retains scalar actions, and the total derived $R\lim$ is obtained by the additive $O$-linear limit on K-injective towers. Hence the realized integral comparison is $O$-linear.

source.place: Actual integral construction in def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image; finite-free natural total-limit comparison.

proof.text: For completeness, the cofinal total-limit identification used in step 6 is the one in the exceptional construction, not a reconstruction from finite evaluations. After forgetting to fixed completed coefficients, restriction $U$ to indices $en$ has the exact left adjoint $L$ which repeats $N_n$ at indices $e(n-1)<m\le en$. The adjunction follows by propagating the map at $en$ backwards within its block. For an acyclic complex $H$, $\operatorname{Hom}(H,UI)=\operatorname{Hom}(LH,I)$ is acyclic if $I$ is K-injective, since $L$ is exact. Thus $U$ preserves K-injectives. Ordinary inverse limits agree: a compatible retained family extends at $m$ by transition from any $en\ge m$, independently of the choice. Computing on $I$ therefore gives the natural cofinal isomorphism for the total derived limit of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. The compatible-family formula commutes with every tower map, with finite-free tensor and with further restriction. It therefore preserves the scalar square and the associator equations from step 4. This is the cofinal realization prescribed in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image].

source.place: Construction 4.1; explicit cofinal K-injective calculation in the exceptional definition.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization] to the integral comparison and its inverse, using step 6's $O$-linearity. By [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] these localized functors are exactly $Lj_i^*Rg_E^!$ and $R(g_i)_E^!$. On a localized arrow $u\otimes a$, the comparison's naturality is the integral naturality equation for $u$, multiplied by $a$. Thus it is a natural isomorphism on the raw localized category, with no idempotent completion. The localization lemma preserves whiskering, composition and comparison-square equations, so steps 3–7 give precisely the finite-field-extension squares for these rational functors, including identity and successive-extension coherence.

source.place: Ancestor section invariant, scalar coefficient clause; rational operation definitions.

proof.text: In the common-stage category of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], let $P=Lj_i^*Rg^!$, $Q=R(g_i)^!$ and write their extension comparisons as $\theta_P:T P_E\cong P_L T$, $\theta_Q:T Q_E\cong Q_L T$. Step 8 says $\theta_Q T\rho_E=\rho_L\theta_P$. Define the component at $(E,K)$ by the class of $\rho_{E,K}$. For an arrow represented by $u:T K\to T K'$ over a common field $L$, its image under either operation is conjugated by that operation's $\theta$ as in the two operation definitions. Substitute the displayed square at both endpoints; the conjugating $\theta$ factors cancel, and naturality becomes $Q_L(u)\rho_{L,TK}=\rho_{L,TK'}P_L(u)$. This holds by step 8. If two representatives agree over $L'$, extend this equation to $L'$; step 8's extension compatibility identifies both images there. Thus the map is independent of representative and common field. The classes of $\rho_E^{-1}$ give the inverse, since their two composites are identity already over $E$.

source.place: Ancestor section invariant; explicit common-stage morphism rule and scalar-compatible descent.

proof.text: Evaluate the established natural comparisons at the coefficient unit $\Lambda_Y$. The exceptional definition gives $G_g\Lambda_Y=\omega_g$ and $G_{g_i}\Lambda_Y=\omega_{g_i}$. Scalar extension carries $\Lambda_Y$ to the target unit by $1\otimes b\mapsto b$, so evaluating the scalar square gives the asserted square for dualizing objects, with the same tensor associators. Restriction preserves the unit by [lem-pur-finite-clopen-derived-decomposition]. If $X_i=\varnothing$, its module category has only the zero sheaf (the empty covering forces its section module to be zero); its strict-system and derived categories are therefore zero. Every component comparison is the unique zero-to-zero arrow at finite and integral stages and after localization or common-stage passage. If $I=\varnothing$, then $X=\varnothing$ and there is no index $i$ and hence no component comparison to assert.

source.place: Ancestor section invariant: evaluation at the coefficient unit and empty-component cases.
